matcher: Deterministic keyword classifier, no LLM. Normalize the question and return the fallback if a fenced phrase appears. Next, if a departureRoutes term appears (a why-did-you-leave question), return its entry only when the question also names one of its requiresAny phrases (Atlas UP); otherwise return the fallback. Then score each entry's priorityKeywords (each matched phrase adds its word count); if any matched, the highest score wins, and a tie goes to the entry listed first. Otherwise return an entry whose question or variant matches exactly, otherwise score keywords the same way. contextKeywords only break ties between the top keyword scores, or decide when no keyword matched. Ties then go to the entry listed first. No score returns the fallback. An entry won only through contextKeywords shows its contextAnswer when it has one. An entry with approved: false is treated as the fallback, so only answers Travis has approved are ever shown. An entry with fallbackOnly: true always returns the fallback; it exists only so its questions are caught before other entries' keywords. Every other answer shows its sourceSections. Entries with suggest: false are never shown as suggested or example questions, and the matched question text is never echoed back.

entries.answer: Using my agentic system at Atlas UP, I cleared a backlog of 100+ bugs and about 25 features in about six weeks, with roughly 95% of bug tickets accepted without being bounced back. The AI regression lane I built also cut a full regression cycle from about a week to 8 to 10 hours.

entries.question: How do you keep an AI product safe for kids?
variants: What is the six-layer safety pipeline?
entries.answer: In FoundrKids, I put every model call through a six-layer safety pipeline: a blocklist, OpenAI moderation, prompt scaffolding, the model, a streaming sentence buffer, and a PII-redacting output filter. It fails closed, and critical events end the session and alert the parent. COPPA is built into the data layer: verified parental consent, a 90-day chat purge, real child deletion, and a tamper-proof audit log.

entries.question: What is FoundrKids?
entries.answer: FoundrKids is an AI maker-learning platform for kids 7 to 15, in pre-launch: a chat coach guides build missions while parents track safety. I'm the founder and sole engineer, and I built the full stack solo: three Vue 3 apps, a FastAPI backend with 140+ endpoints, Postgres with pgvector, Redis, and Stripe on Fly.io and Neon, plus an adaptive learning engine and about 2,500 tests. Model calls route between Anthropic and OpenAI by mission tier, with cross-vendor failover and a monthly spend cap per household.

entries.question: How did you keep the agents safe?
variants: What happens when an agent touches billing or auth?
entries.answer: I designed the safety model that every automated action ran inside. A separate agent verified every fix with fresh context, retries were capped by risk tier, sensitive areas such as billing and auth always stopped for a human, and a global kill switch paused all loops. Separately, on the EOS One MCP server I helped build, destructive actions such as deletes were deliberately excluded, so they had to happen in the app.

Separately, I built an autonomous pull request review agent on Azure DevOps that reviewed open PRs at their latest commit and posted severity-ranked findings, encoding team standards so I was no longer the mandatory manual review gate.
